neighbours.label: The adjective 'quaint' before a place or object
fire: We stayed in a quaint cottage beside the river.
A quaint bakery stood at the end of the lane.
They admired the quaint wooden clock in the hall.
The village has a quaint square with a stone fountain.
She photographed a quaint shop near the harbor.
We ate lunch in a quaint inn outside the town.
Visitors enjoy the quaint houses along the canal.
He bought a quaint lamp at the village market.
quiet: We stayed in a charming cottage beside the river.
A charming bakery stood at the end of the lane.
They admired the old-fashioned wooden clock in the hall.
The village has a picturesque square with a stone fountain.
She photographed a rustic shop near the harbor.
We ate lunch in a cozy inn outside the town.
Visitors enjoy the charming houses along the canal.
He bought an old-fashioned lamp at the village market.

notes: Broad positive pole (1.397% above 0.1 of max); other evocative adjectives also peak. Narrow lexical test with descriptive synonyms as near misses. Labels use the card and top 16 corpus examples. No downloaded band scan covers this neuron. Test sentences were authored by Codex, not Bonsai.
